S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).

subtypes.Animal Type: Marked fear of animals or insects like dogs, bees, snakes, or spiders.
subtypes.Natural Environment Type: Marked fear of the natural environment like storms, heights, water, or the dark.
subtypes.Blood-Injection-Injury Type: Marked fear of seeing blood, receiving injections, or medical procedures.
subtypes.Situational Type: Marked fear of specific situations like airplanes, elevators, tunnels, bridges, or enclosed spaces.
subtypes.Other Type: Marked fear of other situations like choking, vomiting, loud sounds, or costumed characters.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Anticipatory Anxiety: Strong anxiety triggered just by thinking about the possibility of encountering the phobic object.
subtypes.Immediate Panic Response: Overwhelming fear erupting immediately upon facing the phobic object.
subtypes.Physiological Panic Symptoms: Intense physical reactions such as heart palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, or trembling.
subtypes.Freezing: Feeling paralyzed or unable to move due to extreme fear.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Active Avoidance: Intentionally and completely staying away from contact with the phobic object or situation.
subtypes.Functional Impairment due to Avoidance: Accepting severe restrictions on daily life, job, or social activities to avoid the phobic object.
subtypes.Enduring with Distress: Forcing oneself to endure the situation while experiencing intense fear and anxiety because it cannot be avoided.
subtypes.Reliance on Safety Signals: Barely enduring the exposure by relying on a companion or safety object.

symptom.disease_info: Specific Phobia is characterized by a marked, persistent fear of a clearly identifiable object or situation (e.g., animals, heights, flying, injections) that is excessive or out of proportion to the actual danger. Exposure almost invariably elicits an immediate fear response and leads to active avoidance or intense distress, with the fear lasting at least six months and causing significant interference in daily functioning or role obligations. Onset is often in childhood or early adulthood but can emerge after a discrete traumatic or panic-like experience later in life, and the course tends to be chronic if untreated, although the fear is typically circumscribed rather than broad and pervasive. It is distinguished from social anxiety disorder, agoraphobia, and PTSD by the narrow focus on a specific object/situation, absence of pervasive social or situational avoidance patterns, and lack of re-experiencing phenomena.

patient.personality: Josefina is a disciplined yet creatively impulsive culinary manager who leads assertively while harboring a tendency to worry and channel stress into late-night creative pursuits.
patient.stressor: Two years ago, while driving home late from one of her restaurants after a long shift and a menu planning session, Josefina was involved in a minor but frightening bridge incident when a truck ahead lost part of its load; she narrowly avoided a serious collision, scraping the guardrail and coming to a stop with a clear view over the water below. Although she was physically unharmed, the combination of darkness, the sense of height over the river, and the chaos of police and tow trucks left a strong impression on her. Over the following months, she increasingly changed her routes to avoid that and other bridges, rearranged delivery schedules so she wouldn’t have to cross elevated overpasses, and started relying on assistants to cover site visits that required such drives, complicating staffing and limiting her presence at some locations. When a new flagship restaurant opportunity required frequent crossings of a large highway bridge and she realized her avoidance was jeopardizing both the expansion and her reputation for hands-on leadership, she decided she needed professional help.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’ve become overwhelmingly afraid of driving over bridges, even short ones, and it’s starting to control my work.”

S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).
S062.manifestation: Ever since that night on the bridge, the idea of driving over any bridge, even the little one by my house, makes my stomach drop and my hands sweat like I’m about to go off the edge into the water, even though I know in my head it’s a solid road and people do it every day.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.
S063.manifestation: If I’m coming up on a bridge by mistake, my heart starts pounding, my chest feels tight, and I get this rush of heat and dizziness so fast that I have to grip the wheel and fight the urge to slam on the brakes or pull over right there.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.
S064.manifestation: I’ll go twenty minutes out of my way, juggle delivery routes, or make my assistants handle site visits just so I don’t have to cross a bridge, and on the rare times I can’t avoid it I crawl across in the slow lane, white-knuckled, barely breathing, and praying for it to be over.
